references.text: This verse in 2 Chronicles refers directly to the fulfillment of the prophecy in Leviticus 26:35, where the land rested for seventy years during the exile in Babylon so that the sabbatical years which were not kept could be fulfilled.

Describes the sabbatical year (the seventh year) when the land was to rest, which is the basis for the warning in Leviticus 26:35 that the land will receive its rest if Israel does not keep the sabbatical years.
The preceding verse that introduces the theme that the land shall enjoy its sabbatical years while the people are in exile and the land lies desolate.
Repeats the theme that the land shall lie desolate and receive its sabbatical years, explaining that this happens because the people rejected the Lord's laws.
Jeremiah's prophecy that the land will lie desolate for seventy years, which connects to the fulfillment of the sabbath rest for the land mentioned in Leviticus 26:35.
Daniel understands from Jeremiah's writings that the seventy years for Jerusalem's destruction were about to be fulfilled, relating to the land's sabbatical rest.
